HIGH λLambda user acceptance testingio-credential-s3-tst-custom-resource-existing-s3 EOL Runtime Node.js 16 (nodejs16.x) is EOL — unpatched CVEs, future deployments at risk — ▸

Metrics last 28 days

Invocations0
Avg Duration0 ms
Errors0
Throttles0
Configured Memory1024 MB
Last Modified617 days ago
Runtimenodejs16.x
recommendedRuntimenodejs22.x
What does this mean?
AWS has stopped releasing security patches for this software version. Any CVE (security vulnerability) published after the end-of-life date is permanently unpatched in this function. These appear as open findings in security audits and can block compliance certifications.

Recommendation

Node.js 16 (nodejs16.x) has reached end-of-life. AWS no longer ships security patches for this runtime — any known CVEs in the runtime itself will remain unpatched indefinitely. AWS will eventually block new deployments on EOL runtimes, which means your next release could fail silently in CI/CD. Steps to fix: 1. Update your CDK/SAM/serverless.yml — change runtime from nodejs16.x to nodejs22.x 2. Test locally — the function code rarely needs changes unless it uses APIs removed in the new runtime 3. Deploy and verify the function still behaves correctly Target: nodejs22.x
arn:aws:lambda:us-east-1:862996428237:function:io-credential-s3-tst-custom-resource-existing-s3

Fix Command

aws lambda update-function-configuration \
  --function-name "io-credential-s3-tst-custom-resource-existing-s3" \
  --runtime nodejs22.x
# If managed by CDK / SAM / Serverless Framework, update your IaC and redeploy instead

Metrics last 28 days

actualPeakConcurrency0
Configured Memory1024 MB

monthlyCostUsd12.04
What does this mean?
Provisioned Concurrency keeps instances warm to eliminate cold starts — but this function has had zero invocations. You are paying for warm instances that are never invoked.

Recommendation

Remove provisioned concurrency entirely. Re-enable only if traffic resumes. Cold starts will add ~100–500 ms latency but there is no point paying for warm capacity that is never used.
